title: FAA Part 107 airspace practice questions
description: Free FAA Part 107 airspace practice questions on 14 CFR 107.41-107.47 and airspace classes. Every answer is explained and linked to its source.

questions.question: Which airspace does 107.41 list as requiring prior authorization from Air Traffic Control (ATC) before a small unmanned aircraft is operated there?

options.A: Class A and Class G airspace only
options.B: Class B, Class C or Class D airspace, and the surface area of Class E airspace designated for an airport
options.C: Any airspace above 400 feet AGL, whatever its class
options.D: Federal Airways within Class E airspace only

questions.explanation: 107.41 covers "Class B, Class C, or Class D airspace or within the lateral boundaries of the surface area of Class E airspace designated for an airport" and requires "prior authorization from Air Traffic Control (ATC)."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.41, Operation in certain airspace (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No person may operate a small unmanned aircraft in Class B, Class C, or Class D airspace or within the lateral boundaries of the surface area of Class E airspace designated for an airport unless that person has prior authorization from Air Traffic Control (ATC).

questions.question: Under 107.41, whose prior authorization does a person need to operate a small unmanned aircraft in Class D airspace?

options.A: The airport manager
options.B: The local police department
options.C: Air Traffic Control (ATC)
options.D: The nearest Flight Service station

questions.explanation: 107.41 bars operation in Class D airspace "unless that person has prior authorization from Air Traffic Control (ATC)."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.41, Operation in certain airspace (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No person may operate a small unmanned aircraft in Class B, Class C, or Class D airspace or within the lateral boundaries of the surface area of Class E airspace designated for an airport unless that person has prior authorization from Air Traffic Control (ATC).

questions.question: Which part of Class E airspace does 107.41 cover?

options.A: All Class E airspace from 700 feet AGL upward
options.B: Only Class E airspace above 14,500 feet MSL
options.C: Only the Federal Airways within Class E airspace
options.D: The airspace within the lateral boundaries of the surface area of Class E airspace designated for an airport

questions.explanation: 107.41 names the airspace "within the lateral boundaries of the surface area of Class E airspace designated for an airport".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.41, Operation in certain airspace (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No person may operate a small unmanned aircraft in Class B, Class C, or Class D airspace or within the lateral boundaries of the surface area of Class E airspace designated for an airport unless that person has prior authorization from Air Traffic Control (ATC).

questions.question: What does 107.43 prohibit?

options.A: Operating a small unmanned aircraft in a manner that interferes with operations and traffic patterns at any airport, heliport, or seaplane base
options.B: Operating a small unmanned aircraft from any airport property
options.C: Operating a small unmanned aircraft while an airport's control tower is closed
options.D: Operating a small unmanned aircraft over any public-use runway

questions.explanation: 107.43: "No person may operate a small unmanned aircraft in a manner that interferes with operations and traffic patterns at any airport, heliport, or seaplane base."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.43, Operation in the vicinity of airports (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No person may operate a small unmanned aircraft in a manner that interferes with operations and traffic patterns at any airport, heliport, or seaplane base.

questions.question: Which facilities does 107.43 name when it prohibits interference with operations and traffic patterns?

options.A: Airports with an operating control tower only
options.B: Any airport, heliport, or seaplane base
options.C: Public-use airports in Class B airspace only
options.D: Military airfields only

questions.explanation: 107.43 protects operations and traffic patterns "at any airport, heliport, or seaplane base."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.43, Operation in the vicinity of airports (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No person may operate a small unmanned aircraft in a manner that interferes with operations and traffic patterns at any airport, heliport, or seaplane base.

questions.question: Under 107.45, what must a person have to operate a small unmanned aircraft in a prohibited or restricted area?

options.A: A Federal Airways clearance from Flight Service
options.B: Written consent from the nearest landowner
options.C: Permission from the using or controlling agency, as appropriate
options.D: A NOTAM published by the person

questions.explanation: 107.45 bars operation in prohibited or restricted areas "unless that person has permission from the using or controlling agency, as appropriate."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.45, Operation in prohibited or restricted areas (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No person may operate a small unmanned aircraft in prohibited or restricted areas unless that person has permission from the using or controlling agency, as appropriate.

questions.question: Which provisions does 107.47 require a person acting as remote pilot in command to comply with?

options.A: §§ 91.137 through 91.145 and 99.7 of 14 CFR
options.B: §§ 91.103 and 91.111 of 14 CFR only
options.C: Part 89 of 14 CFR only

questions.explanation: 107.47: "A person acting as a remote pilot in command must comply with the provisions of §§ 91.137 through 91.145 and 99.7 of this chapter."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.47, Flight restrictions in the proximity of certain areas designated by notice to airmen (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: A person acting as a remote pilot in command must comply with the provisions of §§ 91.137 through 91.145 and 99.7 of this chapter.

questions.question: What two categories of airspace does the FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide describe?

options.A: Domestic and international
options.B: Visual and instrument
options.C: Civil and military
options.D: Regulatory and nonregulatory

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "The two categories of airspace are: regulatory and nonregulatory."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: The two categories of airspace are: regulatory and nonregulatory.

questions.question: Which four types of airspace does the Study Guide list within the two airspace categories?

options.A: Controlled, uncontrolled, special use, and other airspace
options.B: Class A, Class B, Class C and Class D
options.C: Terminal, en route, oceanic and polar
options.D: Low, medium, high and very high altitude

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "there are four types: controlled, uncontrolled, special use, and other airspace."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Within these two categories, there are four types: controlled, uncontrolled, special use, and other airspace.

questions.topic: Class B, C and D airspace
questions.question: According to the Study Guide, Class B airspace generally extends from the surface to what altitude?

options.A: 2,500 feet above the airport elevation
options.B: 4,000 feet above the airport elevation
options.C: 10,000 feet MSL
options.D: 18,000 feet MSL

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "Class B airspace is generally airspace from the surface to 10,000 feet mean sea level (MSL) surrounding the nation's busiest airports".

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Class B airspace is generally airspace from the surface to 10,000 feet mean sea level (MSL) surrounding the nation's busiest airports

questions.topic: Class B, C and D airspace
questions.question: According to the Study Guide, Class C airspace generally extends from the surface to what height?

options.A: 1,200 feet AGL
options.B: 4,000 feet above the airport elevation (charted in MSL)
options.C: 10,000 feet MSL
options.D: 14,500 feet MSL

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "Class C airspace is generally airspace from the surface to 4,000 feet above the airport elevation (charted in MSL)".

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Class C airspace is generally airspace from the surface to 4,000 feet above the airport elevation (charted in MSL)

questions.topic: Class B, C and D airspace
questions.question: How does the Study Guide describe Class D airspace?

options.A: Generally from the surface to 2,500 feet above the airport elevation (charted in MSL), surrounding airports that have an operational control tower
options.B: Generally from 1,200 feet AGL to 18,000 feet MSL over open country
options.C: All airspace from 18,000 feet MSL up to FL 600
options.D: Airspace over the busiest airports, built in two or more layers

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "Class D airspace is generally airspace from the surface to 2,500 feet above the airport elevation (charted in MSL) surrounding those airports that have an operational control tower."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Class D airspace is generally airspace from the surface to 2,500 feet above the airport elevation (charted in MSL) surrounding those airports that have an operational control tower.

questions.topic: Class B, C and D airspace
questions.question: What radius does the Study Guide give for the surface area that Class C airspace usually consists of?

options.A: Two nautical miles
options.B: Three nautical miles
options.C: Ten nautical miles
options.D: Five nautical miles

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says Class C airspace "usually consists of a surface area with a five nautical mile (NM) radius, an outer circle with a ten NM radius".

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: the airspace usually consists of a surface area with a five nautical mile (NM) radius, an outer circle with a ten NM radius

questions.topic: Class E, Class G and the Class A floor
questions.question: According to the Study Guide, where charts do not depict a Class E base, at what altitude does Class E airspace begin?

options.A: 700 feet AGL
options.B: 1,200 feet AGL
options.C: 14,500 feet MSL
options.D: 18,000 feet MSL

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "In areas where charts do not depict a class E base, class E begins at 14,500 feet MSL."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: In areas where charts do not depict a class E base, class E begins at 14,500 feet MSL.

questions.topic: Class E, Class G and the Class A floor
questions.question: How does the Study Guide define Class G airspace?

options.A: The airspace above FL 600
options.B: The portion of the airspace that has not been designated as Class A, B, C, D, or E
options.C: The controlled airspace not classified as Class A, B, C, or D
options.D: The airspace within 5 NM of an airport without a control tower

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "Uncontrolled airspace or Class G airspace is the portion of the airspace that has not been designated as Class A, B, C, D, or E."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Uncontrolled airspace or Class G airspace is the portion of the airspace that has not been designated as Class A, B, C, D, or E.

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, how is a prohibited area charted?

options.A: As an "R" followed by a number
options.B: As a "P" followed by a number (e.g., P-40)
options.C: As a "W" followed by a number
options.D: By name only, without a number

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "The area is charted as a "P" followed by a number (e.g., P-40)."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: The area is charted as a "P" followed by a number (e.g., P-40).

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, from what distance off the U.S. coast does a warning area extend outward?

options.A: 12 NM
options.B: 1 NM
options.C: 50 NM
options.D: 3 NM

questions.explanation: The Study Guide describes a warning area as "extending from 3 NM outward from the coast of the United States".

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: A warning area is airspace of defined dimensions, extending from 3 NM outward from the coast of the United States

questions.question: What does the Study Guide name as the difference between controlled firing areas (CFAs) and other special use airspace?

options.A: CFAs are always charted with a "C" followed by a number
options.B: CFAs are closed to all aircraft at all times
options.C: Activities must be suspended when a spotter aircraft, radar, or ground lookout position indicates an aircraft might be approaching the area
options.D: CFAs exist only over international waters

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "The difference between CFAs and other special use airspace is that activities must be suspended when a spotter aircraft, radar, or ground lookout position indicates an aircraft might be approaching the area."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: The difference between CFAs and other special use airspace is that activities must be suspended when a spotter aircraft, radar, or ground lookout position indicates an aircraft might be approaching the area.

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what is issued to designate a temporary flight restriction (TFR)?

options.A: A flight data center (FDC) Notice to Airmen (NOTAM)
options.B: A sectional chart revision
options.C: A pilot report (PIREP)
options.D: An entry in the Chart Supplement U.S.

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "A flight data center (FDC) Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) is issued to designate a TFR."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: A flight data center (FDC) Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) is issued to designate a TFR.

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, how are military training routes (MTRs) with no segment above 1,500 feet AGL identified?

options.A: By three number characters (e.g., IR206)
options.B: By name only (e.g., "Camden Ridge")
options.C: By an "A" followed by a number
options.D: By four number characters (e.g., IR1206, VR1207)

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "MTRs with no segment above 1,500 feet AGL are identified by four number characters (e.g., IR1206, VR1207)."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: MTRs with no segment above 1,500 feet AGL are identified by four number characters (e.g., IR1206, VR1207).
